body: IPO July 2004 at $14. Highly levered (securitised debt), it hit ~$3 in Nov 2008 [unverified] and was in the low single digits in early 2009. Dec 2009: CEO-elect Patrick Doyle (CEO Mar 2010) launched the ~$75m 'Pizza Turnaround' campaign on camera admitting customers found the pizza poor, with a new recipe; same-store sales jumped ~14% in Q1 2010 [unverified]. Then a digital-first strategy (Pizza Tracker 2008, online/app ordering, later >half of US sales digital), store remodels, and a 'fortressing' franchise model. Under Doyle the stock rose ~13x (Restaurant Business); Quartz noted it beat Google's return from 2010. Peak ~$567 (Dec 2021) [unverified] ≈ ~180x from the 2008 low, ~65x from 2010. Split: mostly EPS + aggressive buybacks/recaps (negative equity, share count down); P/E moved from ~10x to ~30x+ [unverified]. Drawdown: ~-80% 2007-08 pre-turnaround [unverified]; -~35% 2022. EARLY SIGNAL visible in 2010: the honest relaunch produced an immediate double-digit same-store-sales jump — a measurable demand response — at a ~10x P/E. Who caught it: few documented; later Berkshire Hathaway disclosed a DPZ stake (Q3 2024). Stall: 2022-26 range-bound as US delivery competition and aggregators matured. LESSON: in a franchise model, a product reset that shows up in same-store sales within one quarter, plus leverage-funded buybacks, can produce a 100x; check the first comp print.

data.early_signals: Q1 2010 same-store sales jump after honest relaunch; digital ordering share
data.lesson: first comp print after product reset is the signal

title: Domino's Pizza 2008-2021: 'our pizza was bad' turnaround, ~180x from trough
